pattern-selector.why: the forces are a missing read-only predicate over an existing installer; the fit is one verdict branch over the plan the installer already computes, deliberately no new gate class or re-derivation.
pattern-selector.what: added a --check flag and a verdict branch; recorded the rejected separate-gate option in ADR-0115.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: building the --check mode ADR-0110 specified is a decision a maintainer will question (why reuse the installer, why read-only, why the bot stays separate).
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0115 (reuse the plan, read-only, exit verdicts, the rejected separate gate, limits), referencing ADR-0110 for the bot.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the new verdict behavior (covered, drift, un-gated-read-only, bad-source-fail-closed) is enumerated as Gherkin for the operator and agent audiences and logged.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added an executable feature with four scenarios and a steps file that genesis's a throwaway consumer and runs the real --check, plus a coverage-log entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the defect class is installer-to-tree coverage, so the tests run the real esk-genesis end to end against fixture consumer repos, not a unit of the predicate.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added five node:test CHECK cases (covered 0, drift 1, un-gated 1 and writes nothing, bad-source 2, read-only wins).
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: a --check that went blind would ship green, so its tests must fail when the check is neutralized.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: mutation pass: forced checkMode=false and confirmed all five CHECK cases go red; restored; recorded in the review entry.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the claim that gap 2 could be closed in-repo was disconfirmed: nothing committed in one repo can enforce another, so only the --check predicate is committable here and the cross-repo bot stays governance-repo work.
skeptical-audit.what: recorded that honest limit in ADR-0115 (a repo that wires nothing is still un-gated; --check does not verify the applied ruleset).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the change edits the installer that writes a consumer's enforcement, so it got a fresh-context four-question review over both changed code files.
judge-arch.what: a fresh-context subagent reviewed esk-genesis.mjs and the test, confirming --check cannot write and fails closed; review recorded.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the simplest thing that meets the requirement (a branchable coverage predicate) is reusing the installer's existing nothingToDo plan, not a second gate that re-derives which gates belong.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept --check to one flag and one verdict branch reusing nothingToDo and the hash checks, so there is one owner of coverage; documented it in bootstrap SKILL.md.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, or production rollout; --check reports whether a repo's CI gates are installed, it does not change what runs in production.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, retention, or migration; a read-only coverage verdict over local files.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no untrusted input, auth, secret, or network surface; --check reads the local source/target trees and spawns git with argument arrays (no shell string built from file content).

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert; a build-time CLI predicate.

arch-encode.why: the coverage predicate is a reused installer plan, not a caught source-pattern mistake to encode as an arch-gate grep rule.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; a Node CLI.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the --check output names the verdict (covered / DRIFT / cannot assess) and the fix in plain words.
